pl-l4d20c7-d1e115.summary: Asks whether the offering should be received for one who hastened to penance, could not find a priest, and died, and answers that it should.
claims: Offerings may be made for one who died seeking penance.

pl-l4d20c7-d1e118.summary: Cites the Council of Epaone: if someone dies without having confessed, has a good reputation, and could not reach a priest, death overtaking him at home or on the road, his relatives should make an offering for him at the altar and give ransom for captives.
claims: Relatives should offer at the altar and give alms for such a person.

pl-l4d20c7.summary: Asks whether the offering should be accepted for one who, hurrying to penance, could not find a priest and died. It should: the Council of Epaone says that for one who died unconfessed, of good repute, overtaken by death at home or on the way, his relatives should make an offering at the altar and give ransom for captives.
claims: Offerings may be made for one who died seeking penance without finding a priest.
Relatives should offer at the altar and give alms for him.
